changes.where: How to use this very large guide, P1
changes.before: To make it easier, you can begin with the Quick start section, then learn one of the inductions and the whole return sequence. Then, you can read the Let the next response guide you section, for the part of the practice no recording can decide in advance. You can also look at the daily and weekly sections to make the practice your own. There are lots of appendices with extra tools, covering lots of topics, including asking questions, NLP patterns of language, working with anxiety, working with daydreams, altered states in general, what to do if you experience the sensation of a hostile presence, working with sleep, influence, and more inductions. All sources used are in Appendix K.

changes.before: “How do I do this?” you ask. Just listen. When you warm up to what’s there, protect it, clarify what it is, reality test it, and then act on it, you’ll find that you don’t even need to have a dramatic trance experience to demonstrate the results of all parts of your mind talking to each other and trusting each other more.
changes.after: “How do I do this?” you ask. Just listen silently. Many people skip the listening or shorten it since it's not "achieving something" but this is by far the most important step. When you warm up to what’s there, protect it, clarify what it is, reality test it, and then act on it, you’ll find that you don’t even need to have a dramatic trance experience to demonstrate the results of all parts of your mind talking to each other and trusting each other more.

changes.where: Do you usually think in words?, P2
changes.before: This doesn't mean that in any given moment you won't notice feelings before words. You don’t have to decide that feelings always come first. This isn't a diagnosis, just a way of finding what's useful. "Not sure" is an answer.
changes.after: Keep in mind that it's normal, even for people who do think in words, to sometimes notice feelings before words.
